## numerai
IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS FOR USING THE NUMERAI MCP SERVER:

This server provides several tools for interacting with the Numerai Tournament API.
All functionality is accessed by calling these tools directly — they are already
available in your tool catalog via tools/list. Do NOT call list_mcp_resources or
list_mcp_resource_templates to discover functionality. The tools are already loaded.

When a user asks what you can do with Numerai, or asks about Numerai capabilities,
IMMEDIATELY all tools/list to list these tools and offer to call them. Do not search
for resources first.

TERMINOLOGY:
- "Models" are prediction algorithms submitted by participants
- "Accounts" are people/entities who own models — one account can have many models
- Tournament 8 = "Classic", 11 = "Signals", 12 = "CryptoSignals"

KEY METRICS:
- mmcRep = meta-model contribution reputation (main performance score)
- fncV3Rep = feature-neutral correlation v3 reputation
- return13Weeks = 13-week return on staked NMR
- nmrStaked = NMR cryptocurrency staked on the model
- latestReps = nested object with current reputation scores (corr, mmc, fnc)
- latestRanks = nested object with current rankings
- latestReturns = nested object with return data (oneDay, threeMonths, oneYear)

43	      unzip -q "$tmp/ic.zip" -d /opt/oracle; \
44	      ln -sfn "$(find /opt/oracle -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'instantclient_*' | head -1)" /opt/oracle/instantclient; \

46	      ldconfig; \

# .devcontainer/Dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \
    libgomp1 \
    libaio1 \
    graphviz \
    zsh \
    tmux \
    neovim \
    btop \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Oracle Instant Client (basiclite) — python-oracledb THICK mode needs it.
# TIA QA (tiafsqa) is older than 12.1 and resets THIN connections (DPY-4011),
# so the live pull runs thick, exactly like DBeaver's OCI driver. The pipeline
# reads $ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB (conf/base/parameters.yml -> oracle.lib_dir); we set
# it below and register the lib dir with ldconfig so LD_LIBRARY_PATH is optional.
# libaio1 (installed above) is the only shared-lib dependency.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linuxx64.zip" ;; \
      arm64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linux-arm64.zip" ;; \
      *) url="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$url" ]; then \
      mkdir -p /opt/oracle; \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$tmp/ic.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/ic.zip" -d /opt/oracle; \
      ln -sfn "$(find /opt/oracle -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'instantclient_*' | head -1)" /opt/oracle/instantclient; \
      echo /opt/oracle/instantclient > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/oracle-instantclient.conf; \
      ldconfig; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no Oracle Instant Client build for arch=$arch; thick mode unavailable"; \
    fi
ENV ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB=/opt/oracle/instantclient

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# oh-my-claudecode CLI (system-wide) — provides the `omc` command used to wire
# the HUD statusline / hooks / agents (via `omc setup`) and the HUD npm fallback.
# Matches the host machine's setup; omc self-updates so we track latest.
RUN npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest

# AWS session tooling — so the Azure-federated STS login can be refreshed FROM
# INSIDE this container, not only on the WSL host. The artifact root is S3
# (PSDP_DATA_ROOT) with 12h tokens, so "my session died mid-session" is routine;
# previously it meant dropping out to a host terminal. See scripts/azlogin.
#
#   aws CLI v2       : `aws sts get-caller-identity` is how scripts/az_login.sh
#                      authoritatively verifies a login (the tool's exit code
#                      lies), plus general S3 work against the artifact root.
#   chromium (apt)   : NOT used as the browser — puppeteer ships its own
#                      version-matched build. This is here for its shared-library
#                      dependencies (libnss3/libgbm1/libasound2/…), which that
#                      bundled Chromium needs; the binary is a fallback you can
#                      select with PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium.
#   aws-azure-login  : the SAML login itself. Pinned — 3.6.x is what the login
#                      flow in scripts/az_login.sh is written against.
#
# The npm install is guarded: puppeteer's postinstall is what fetches that
# matched Chromium, and npm 11 already warns that the script is "not yet covered
# by allowScripts". It still runs today, but the day it stops, .local-chromium is
# silently empty and the login breaks at runtime, in the user's terminal, weeks
# later. --foreground-scripts puts the download in the build log and the `test -d`
# turns that failure into a failed image build instead.
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) a="x86_64" ;; \
      arm64) a="aarch64" ;; \
      *) a="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$a" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-${a}.zip" -o "$tmp/awscliv2.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/awscliv2.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      "$tmp/aws/install" --update; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no AWS CLI v2 build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi; \
    npm install -g --foreground-scripts aws-azure-login@3.6.4; \
    test -d /usr/lib/node_modules/aws-azure-login/node_modules/puppeteer/.local-chromium

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Data-pipeline CLI tooling — chosen for THIS project's artifacts:
#   duckdb : SQL straight over the pipeline's parquet/csv/xlsx without Python —
#            e.g. duckdb -c "select status,count(*) from
#            'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1"
#   yq     : query/validate the owned SQL + taxonomy YAML (source_queries /
#            error_taxonomy / scope) from the shell, jq-style.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) duck="amd64"; yqa="amd64" ;; \
      arm64) duck="arm64"; yqa="arm64" ;; \
      *) duck=""; yqa="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$duck" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/latest/download/duckdb_cli-linux-${duck}.zip" -o "$tmp/duckdb.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/duckdb.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$tmp/duckdb" /usr/local/bin/duckdb; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_${yqa}" -o /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no duckdb/yq build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi

# eza / delta / dust (not in Debian stable) + starship prompt.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) t="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      arm64) t="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      *) t="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$t" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/eza-community/eza/releases/latest/download/eza_${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/0.18.2/delta-0.18.2-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/bootandy/dust/releases/download/v1.1.1/dust-v1.1.1-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name eza   | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/eza; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name delta | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/delta; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name dust  | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/dust; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    fi; \
    curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y

RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Runs once on container create/rebuild. Sequential + idempotent so the whole
3	# environment (uv, deps, Claude Code, oh-my-claudecode, HUD, hooks, shell) is
4	# set up automatically with no manual steps. Safe to re-run.
5	set -uo pipefail
6	log() { echo "[post-create] $*"; }
7	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
8	
9	# Canonical OMC marketplace URL — matches the host machine's settings.json.
10	OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL="https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"
11	
12	# 1. uv (for the vscode user; the Dockerfile installs it for root)
13	if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
14	  log "installing uv"
15	  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
16	  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
17	fi
18	
19	# 2. Project dependencies — a project-local .venv the scripts/launch.json expect
20	#    (.venv/bin/python). Install the package editable with the dev + notebooks
21	#    extras, plus oracledb (thick-mode driver for the live TIA/Oracle pull; it
22	#    is imported by src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/.../oracle_source.py but not pinned in the
23	#    project metadata, so we add it explicitly). This mirrors the working host
24	#    venv (kedro-viz, plotly, ipykernel, pytest, s3fs, oracledb all present).
25	if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then
26	  log "creating .venv (python 3.12)"
27	  uv venv --python 3.12 || log "WARN: uv venv failed"
28	  log "installing project + dev,notebooks extras + oracledb"
29	  uv pip install -e ".[dev,notebooks]" oracledb || log "WARN: dependency install failed"
30	fi
31	
32	# 2b. VisiData — interactive terminal explorer for the pipeline's data artifacts
33	#     (parquet findings/intermediates, xlsx golden masters, csv drilldowns).
34	#     Installed isolated via `uv tool` so it never touches the project venv.
35	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
36	  log "installing visidata (uv tool)"
37	  uv tool install 'visidata[parquet]' 2>/dev/null \
38	    || uv tool install visidata \
39	    || log "WARN: visidata install failed (non-fatal)"
40	fi
41	
42	# 2d. nbstripout git filter — .gitattributes marks *.ipynb/*.zpln with
43	#     filter=nbstripout, but the clean/smudge commands live in the per-clone
44	#     .git/config (not the repo). Point them at THIS container's .venv python so
45	#     notebook outputs are stripped on commit. `--install` is idempotent and
46	#     rewrites any stale absolute path from a previous machine. nbstripout ships
47	#     in the notebooks extra installed above.
48	if [ -f pyproject.toml ] && [ -x .venv/bin/python ] && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
49	  log "configuring nbstripout git filter (.venv)"
50	  .venv/bin/python -m nbstripout --install --attributes .gitattributes \
51	    || log "WARN: nbstripout filter install failed"
52	fi
53	
54	# 3. Claude Code (install or update to latest)
55	log "installing/updating Claude Code (latest)"
56	curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash || log "WARN: claude install failed"
57	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
58	
59	# 4. oh-my-claudecode plugin (latest) — provides the /oh-my-claudecode:* skills
60	if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
61	  log "setting up oh-my-claudecode plugin"
62	  claude plugin marketplace add "$OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL" || log "WARN: omc marketplace add failed"
63	  claude plugin marketplace update omc || true
64	  claude plugin install oh-my-claudecode@omc || log "WARN: omc plugin install failed"
65	else
66	  log "WARN: claude not on PATH; skipping oh-my-claudecode plugin"
67	fi
68	
69	# 5. omc CLI + `omc setup` — installs the HUD statusline wrapper, hooks, agents
70	#    and skills into ~/.claude (the piece that gives the host its HUD niceties).
71	#    The CLI is baked into the image (Dockerfile); install per-user if missing.
72	if ! command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
73	  log "installing omc CLI (oh-my-claude-sisyphus)"
74	  npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest 2>/dev/null \
75	    || sudo npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
76	    || log "WARN: omc CLI install failed"
77	fi
78	if command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
79	  log "running omc setup (HUD + hooks + agents + skills)"
80	  omc setup --quiet || log "WARN: omc setup failed"
81	else
82	  log "WARN: omc CLI unavailable; HUD/hooks may be incomplete"
83	fi
84	
85	# 6. pre-commit git hooks (only if the repo defines them)
86	if [ -f .pre-commit-config.yaml ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
87	  log "installing pre-commit hooks"
88	  uv run pre-commit install || log "WARN: pre-commit install failed"
89	fi
90	
91	# 6a. Azure CLI + azure-devops extension — the repo lives on
92	#     dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice, so `az repos pr` / `az pipelines` /
93	#     `az boards` is the terminal path to PRs, builds and work items
94	#     (gh only speaks GitHub). Idempotent: skipped when already installed.
95	if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
96	  log "installing Azure CLI"
97	  curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash || log "WARN: azure-cli install failed"
98	fi
99	if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! az extension show --name azure-devops >/dev/null 2>&1; then
100	  log "adding azure-devops extension"
101	  az extension add --name azure-devops || log "WARN: azure-devops extension install failed"
102	fi
103	
104	# 6b. Azure DevOps CLI defaults — org/project set once so no command needs
105	#     flags. Auth: export AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (e.g. via the repo's .env) for
106	#     non-interactive use, or `az login` / `az devops login` interactively.
107	if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
108	  log "configuring az devops org/project defaults"
109	  az devops configure --defaults \
110	    organization=https://dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice \
111	    "project=Data Science and Advanced Analytics" \
112	    || log "WARN: az devops configure failed"
113	else
114	  log "WARN: az not on PATH (azure-cli feature missing?); skipping ADO defaults"
115	fi
116	
117	# 6c. Azure DevOps aliases — oh-my-zsh sources every $ZSH_CUSTOM/*.zsh file.
118	ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR="${ZSH_CUSTOM:-$HOME/.oh-my-zsh/custom}"
119	if [ -d "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR" ]; then
120	  log "writing azure-devops aliases ($ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh)"
121	  cat > "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh" <<'EOF'
122	# Azure DevOps shortcuts (org/project defaults set by post-create.sh)
123	alias adopr='az repos pr create --draft --open'      # current branch -> draft PR
124	alias adoprs='az repos pr list --status active -o table'
125	alias adoruns='az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table'
126	EOF
127	fi
128	
129	# 7. Handy command cheatsheet (shown by ~/.zshrc on interactive login)
130	mkdir -p ~/.config/dev-bootstrap
131	cat > ~/.config/dev-bootstrap/commands.txt <<'EOF'
132	source .venv/bin/activate            # activate the project venv
133	scripts/run.sh offline               # rebuild ledgers + deliverables (no DB)
134	scripts/run.sh full                  # live TIA + Django pull -> ledgers -> deliverables
135	kedro run --pipeline figures         # just redraw the two infographics
136	kedro viz                            # interactive pipeline graph (port 4141, auto-forwarded)
137	scripts/run_notebooks.sh             # rerun the audit notebooks (notebook<->pipeline smoke test)
138	pytest -q                            # reconciliation + source-contract gates
139	python -m policy_schedule_data_pipeline.core.data_paths          # which window/pull is current
140	duckdb -c "select outcome, count(*) n from 'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1 order by n desc"
141	vd data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet                   # browse the ledger (VisiData)
142	yq '.tia_log' src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/reference/source_queries.yaml   # the SQL, as owned data
143	az repos pr create --draft --open    # current branch -> draft PR (alias: adopr)
144	az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table  # recent pipeline runs (alias: adoruns)
145	# A live pull needs TIA_PASSWORD + PG_DJANGO_PROD_PASSWORD (both in .env).
146	# ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB is preset to the Instant Client baked into this image.
147	# NOTE: a full pull re-reads the MUTABLE TIA.POLICY, which re-dates the
148	# landed / phantom / MTA numbers on every artifact. Offline runs never do.
149	EOF
150	
151	# 8. Mirror the host's Claude niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json.
152	#    Merged via jq so existing keys survive. This wires:
153	#      - HUD statusline        - agent teams (needs tmux, in image)
154	#      - vim editor mode       - tmux teammates + fullscreen TUI
155	#      - verbose output        - the OMC plugin + marketplace
156	#    plus bypassPermissions, which is container-specific (sandboxed vscode user).
157	mkdir -p ~/.claude
158	SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
159	[ -s "$SETTINGS" ] || echo '{}' > "$SETTINGS"
160	if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
161	  tmp="$(mktemp)"
162	  jq \
163	    '.permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"
164	     | .env["CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS"] = "1"
165	     | .statusLine = {"type": "command", "command": "node ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hud/omc-hud.mjs"}
166	     | .enabledPlugins["oh-my-claudecode@omc"] = true
167	     | .extraKnownMarketplaces.omc.source = {"source": "git", "url": "https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"}
168	     | .editorMode = "vim"
169	     | .verbose = true
170	     | .teammateMode = "tmux"
171	     | .tui = "fullscreen"' \
172	    "$SETTINGS" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$SETTINGS"
173	  log "merged HUD + OMC niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json"
174	else
175	  log "WARN: jq missing; could not write ~/.claude/settings.json"
176	fi
177	
178	# 9. Shell: link the shared dotfiles (zshrc / starship / tmux) from ~/env.
179	#    ~/env is bind-mounted read-only from the host (see devcontainer.json), so a
180	#    single source of truth drives the host and every container.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs once on container create/rebuild. Sequential + idempotent so the whole
# environment (uv, deps, Claude Code, oh-my-claudecode, HUD, hooks, shell) is
# set up automatically with no manual steps. Safe to re-run.
set -uo pipefail
log() { echo "[post-create] $*"; }
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Canonical OMC marketplace URL — matches the host machine's settings.json.
OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL="https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"

# 1. uv (for the vscode user; the Dockerfile installs it for root)
if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing uv"
  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi

# 2. Project dependencies — a project-local .venv the scripts/launch.json expect
#    (.venv/bin/python). Install the package editable with the dev + notebooks
#    extras, plus oracledb (thick-mode driver for the live TIA/Oracle pull; it
#    is imported by src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/.../oracle_source.py but not pinned in the
#    project metadata, so we add it explicitly). This mirrors the working host
#    venv (kedro-viz, plotly, ipykernel, pytest, s3fs, oracledb all present).
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then
  log "creating .venv (python 3.12)"
  uv venv --python 3.12 || log "WARN: uv venv failed"
  log "installing project + dev,notebooks extras + oracledb"
  uv pip install -e ".[dev,notebooks]" oracledb || log "WARN: dependency install failed"
fi

# 2b. VisiData — interactive terminal explorer for the pipeline's data artifacts
#     (parquet findings/intermediates, xlsx golden masters, csv drilldowns).
#     Installed isolated via `uv tool` so it never touches the project venv.
if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing visidata (uv tool)"
  uv tool install 'visidata[parquet]' 2>/dev/null \
    || uv tool install visidata \
    || log "WARN: visidata install failed (non-fatal)"
fi

# 2d. nbstripout git filter — .gitattributes marks *.ipynb/*.zpln with
#     filter=nbstripout, but the clean/smudge commands live in the per-clone
#     .git/config (not the repo). Point them at THIS container's .venv python so
#     notebook outputs are stripped on commit. `--install` is idempotent and
#     rewrites any stale absolute path from a previous machine. nbstripout ships
#     in the notebooks extra installed above.
if [ -f pyproject.toml ] && [ -x .venv/bin/python ] && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "configuring nbstripout git filter (.venv)"
  .venv/bin/python -m nbstripout --install --attributes .gitattributes \
    || log "WARN: nbstripout filter install failed"
fi

# 3. Claude Code (install or update to latest)
log "installing/updating Claude Code (latest)"
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash || log "WARN: claude install failed"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# 4. oh-my-claudecode plugin (latest) — provides the /oh-my-claudecode:* skills
if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "setting up oh-my-claudecode plugin"
  claude plugin marketplace add "$OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL" || log "WARN: omc marketplace add failed"
  claude plugin marketplace update omc || true
  claude plugin install oh-my-claudecode@omc || log "WARN: omc plugin install failed"
else
  log "WARN: claude not on PATH; skipping oh-my-claudecode plugin"
fi

# 5. omc CLI + `omc setup` — installs the HUD statusline wrapper, hooks, agents
#    and skills into ~/.claude (the piece that gives the host its HUD niceties).
#    The CLI is baked into the image (Dockerfile); install per-user if missing.
if ! command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing omc CLI (oh-my-claude-sisyphus)"
  npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest 2>/dev/null \
    || sudo npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    || log "WARN: omc CLI install failed"
fi
if command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "running omc setup (HUD + hooks + agents + skills)"
  omc setup --quiet || log "WARN: omc setup failed"
else
  log "WARN: omc CLI unavailable; HUD/hooks may be incomplete"
fi

# 6. pre-commit git hooks (only if the repo defines them)
if [ -f .pre-commit-config.yaml ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing pre-commit hooks"
  uv run pre-commit install || log "WARN: pre-commit install failed"
fi

# 6a. Azure CLI + azure-devops extension — the repo lives on
#     dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice, so `az repos pr` / `az pipelines` /
#     `az boards` is the terminal path to PRs, builds and work items
#     (gh only speaks GitHub). Idempotent: skipped when already installed.
if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing Azure CLI"
  curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash || log "WARN: azure-cli install failed"
fi
if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! az extension show --name azure-devops >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "adding azure-devops extension"
  az extension add --name azure-devops || log "WARN: azure-devops extension install failed"
fi

# 6b. Azure DevOps CLI defaults — org/project set once so no command needs
#     flags. Auth: export AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (e.g. via the repo's .env) for
#     non-interactive use, or `az login` / `az devops login` interactively.
if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "configuring az devops org/project defaults"
  az devops configure --defaults \
    organization=https://dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice \
    "project=Data Science and Advanced Analytics" \
    || log "WARN: az devops configure failed"
else
  log "WARN: az not on PATH (azure-cli feature missing?); skipping ADO defaults"
fi

# 6c. Azure DevOps aliases — oh-my-zsh sources every $ZSH_CUSTOM/*.zsh file.
ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR="${ZSH_CUSTOM:-$HOME/.oh-my-zsh/custom}"
if [ -d "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR" ]; then
  log "writing azure-devops aliases ($ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh)"
  cat > "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh" <<'EOF'
# Azure DevOps shortcuts (org/project defaults set by post-create.sh)
alias adopr='az repos pr create --draft --open'      # current branch -> draft PR
alias adoprs='az repos pr list --status active -o table'
alias adoruns='az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table'
EOF
fi

# 7. Handy command cheatsheet (shown by ~/.zshrc on interactive login)
mkdir -p ~/.config/dev-bootstrap
cat > ~/.config/dev-bootstrap/commands.txt <<'EOF'
source .venv/bin/activate            # activate the project venv
scripts/run.sh offline               # rebuild ledgers + deliverables (no DB)
scripts/run.sh full                  # live TIA + Django pull -> ledgers -> deliverables
kedro run --pipeline figures         # just redraw the two infographics
kedro viz                            # interactive pipeline graph (port 4141, auto-forwarded)
scripts/run_notebooks.sh             # rerun the audit notebooks (notebook<->pipeline smoke test)
pytest -q                            # reconciliation + source-contract gates
python -m policy_schedule_data_pipeline.core.data_paths          # which window/pull is current
duckdb -c "select outcome, count(*) n from 'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1 order by n desc"
vd data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet                   # browse the ledger (VisiData)
yq '.tia_log' src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/reference/source_queries.yaml   # the SQL, as owned data
az repos pr create --draft --open    # current branch -> draft PR (alias: adopr)
az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table  # recent pipeline runs (alias: adoruns)
# A live pull needs TIA_PASSWORD + PG_DJANGO_PROD_PASSWORD (both in .env).
# ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB is preset to the Instant Client baked into this image.
# NOTE: a full pull re-reads the MUTABLE TIA.POLICY, which re-dates the
# landed / phantom / MTA numbers on every artifact. Offline runs never do.
EOF

# 8. Mirror the host's Claude niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json.
#    Merged via jq so existing keys survive. This wires:
#      - HUD statusline        - agent teams (needs tmux, in image)
#      - vim editor mode       - tmux teammates + fullscreen TUI
#      - verbose output        - the OMC plugin + marketplace
#    plus bypassPermissions, which is container-specific (sandboxed vscode user).
mkdir -p ~/.claude
SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
[ -s "$SETTINGS" ] || echo '{}' > "$SETTINGS"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  jq \
    '.permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"
     | .env["CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS"] = "1"
     | .statusLine = {"type": "command", "command": "node ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hud/omc-hud.mjs"}
     | .enabledPlugins["oh-my-claudecode@omc"] = true
     | .extraKnownMarketplaces.omc.source = {"source": "git", "url": "https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"}
     | .editorMode = "vim"
     | .verbose = true
     | .teammateMode = "tmux"
     | .tui = "fullscreen"' \
    "$SETTINGS" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$SETTINGS"
  log "merged HUD + OMC niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json"
else
  log "WARN: jq missing; could not write ~/.claude/settings.json"
fi

# 9. Shell: link the shared dotfiles (zshrc / starship / tmux) from ~/env.
#    ~/env is bind-mounted read-only from the host (see devcontainer.json), so a
#    single source of truth drives the host and every container.
ENV_DIR="$HOME/env"
if [ -x "$ENV_DIR/install.sh" ]; then
  log "linking dotfiles from $ENV_DIR"
  "$ENV_DIR/install.sh" --link || log "WARN: dotfile link failed"
else
  log "NOTE: ~/env not mounted; using default shell config"
fi

# 10. zsh-history-substring-search (not packaged on Debian)
HSS="$HOME/.zsh/plugins/zsh-history-substring-search"
[ -d "$HSS" ] || git clone --depth=1 \
  https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-history-substring-search "$HSS" || true

log "done"

# .devcontainer/Dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \
    libgomp1 \
    libaio1 \
    graphviz \
    zsh \
    tmux \
    neovim \
    btop \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Oracle Instant Client (basiclite) — python-oracledb THICK mode needs it.
# TIA QA (tiafsqa) is older than 12.1 and resets THIN connections (DPY-4011),
# so the live pull runs thick, exactly like DBeaver's OCI driver. The pipeline
# reads $ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB (conf/base/parameters.yml -> oracle.lib_dir); we set
# it below and register the lib dir with ldconfig so LD_LIBRARY_PATH is optional.
# libaio1 (installed above) is the only shared-lib dependency.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linuxx64.zip" ;; \
      arm64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linux-arm64.zip" ;; \
      *) url="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$url" ]; then \
      mkdir -p /opt/oracle; \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$tmp/ic.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/ic.zip" -d /opt/oracle; \
      ln -sfn "$(find /opt/oracle -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'instantclient_*' | head -1)" /opt/oracle/instantclient; \
      echo /opt/oracle/instantclient > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/oracle-instantclient.conf; \
      ldconfig; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no Oracle Instant Client build for arch=$arch; thick mode unavailable"; \
    fi
ENV ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB=/opt/oracle/instantclient

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# oh-my-claudecode CLI (system-wide) — provides the `omc` command used to wire
# the HUD statusline / hooks / agents (via `omc setup`) and the HUD npm fallback.
# Matches the host machine's setup; omc self-updates so we track latest.
RUN npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest

# AWS session tooling — so the Azure-federated STS login can be refreshed FROM
# INSIDE this container, not only on the WSL host. The artifact root is S3
# (PSDP_DATA_ROOT) with 12h tokens, so "my session died mid-session" is routine;
# previously it meant dropping out to a host terminal. See scripts/azlogin.
#
#   aws CLI v2       : `aws sts get-caller-identity` is how scripts/az_login.sh
#                      authoritatively verifies a login (the tool's exit code
#                      lies), plus general S3 work against the artifact root.
#   chromium (apt)   : NOT used as the browser — puppeteer ships its own
#                      version-matched build. This is here for its shared-library
#                      dependencies (libnss3/libgbm1/libasound2/…), which that
#                      bundled Chromium needs; the binary is a fallback you can
#                      select with PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium.
#   aws-azure-login  : the SAML login itself. Pinned — 3.6.x is what the login
#                      flow in scripts/az_login.sh is written against.
#
# The npm install is guarded: puppeteer's postinstall is what fetches that
# matched Chromium, and npm 11 already warns that the script is "not yet covered
# by allowScripts". It still runs today, but the day it stops, .local-chromium is
# silently empty and the login breaks at runtime, in the user's terminal, weeks
# later. --foreground-scripts puts the download in the build log and the `test -d`
# turns that failure into a failed image build instead.
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) a="x86_64" ;; \
      arm64) a="aarch64" ;; \
      *) a="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$a" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-${a}.zip" -o "$tmp/awscliv2.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/awscliv2.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      "$tmp/aws/install" --update; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no AWS CLI v2 build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi; \
    npm install -g --foreground-scripts aws-azure-login@3.6.4; \
    test -d /usr/lib/node_modules/aws-azure-login/node_modules/puppeteer/.local-chromium

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Data-pipeline CLI tooling — chosen for THIS project's artifacts:
#   duckdb : SQL straight over the pipeline's parquet/csv/xlsx without Python —
#            e.g. duckdb -c "select status,count(*) from
#            'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1"
#   yq     : query/validate the owned SQL + taxonomy YAML (source_queries /
#            error_taxonomy / scope) from the shell, jq-style.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) duck="amd64"; yqa="amd64" ;; \
      arm64) duck="arm64"; yqa="arm64" ;; \
      *) duck=""; yqa="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$duck" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/latest/download/duckdb_cli-linux-${duck}.zip" -o "$tmp/duckdb.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/duckdb.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$tmp/duckdb" /usr/local/bin/duckdb; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_${yqa}" -o /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq; \

    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \
    libgomp1 \
    libaio1 \
    graphviz \
    zsh \
    tmux \
    neovim \

    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# TIA QA (tiafsqa) is older than 12.1 and resets THIN connections (DPY-4011),
# so the live pull runs thick, exactly like DBeaver's OCI driver. The pipeline
# reads $ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB (conf/base/parameters.yml -> oracle.lib_dir); we set
# it below and register the lib dir with ldconfig so LD_LIBRARY_PATH is optional.
# libaio1 (installed above) is the only shared-lib dependency.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linuxx64.zip" ;; \
      arm64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linux-arm64.zip" ;; \
      *) url="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$url" ]; then \
      mkdir -p /opt/oracle; \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$tmp/ic.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/ic.zip" -d /opt/oracle; \
      ln -sfn "$(find /opt/oracle -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'instantclient_*' | head -1)" /opt/oracle/instantclient; \
      echo /opt/oracle/instantclient > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/oracle-instantclient.conf; \
      ldconfig; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no Oracle Instant Client build for arch=$arch; thick mode unavailable"; \
    fi

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# `claude` and `omc` exist even if post-create fails or is skipped. post-create
# (via scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh) updates both to latest and wires the OMC
# plugin/HUD/hooks; the npm prefix is root-owned so the settings merge disables

    && claude --version \
    && omc --version

# INSIDE this container, not only on the WSL host. The artifact root is S3
# (PSDP_DATA_ROOT) with 12h tokens, so "my session died mid-session" is routine;

#                      version-matched build. This is here for its shared-library

#                      bundled Chromium needs; the binary is a fallback you can
#                      select with PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium.

#                      flow in scripts/az_login.sh is written against.

# turns that failure into a failed image build instead.

    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) a="x86_64" ;; \
      arm64) a="aarch64" ;; \
      *) a="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$a" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-${a}.zip" -o "$tmp/awscliv2.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/awscliv2.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      "$tmp/aws/install" --update; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no AWS CLI v2 build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi; \
    npm install -g --foreground-scripts aws-azure-login@3.6.4; \
    test -d /usr/lib/node_modules/aws-azure-login/node_modules/puppeteer/.local-chromium

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install/update Claude Code + oh-my-claudecode: CLIs, OMC plugin, HUD
# statusline, hooks, and ~/.claude/settings.json niceties.
#
# Called by .devcontainer/post-create.sh on container create, and safe to
# re-run manually any time something looks broken:
#
#   scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh
#
# Both CLIs are also baked into the devcontainer IMAGE (see
# .devcontainer/Dockerfile), so `claude` exists even if this script never ran —
# this script's job is updating to latest and wiring the plugin/HUD/settings.
set -uo pipefail
log() { echo "[setup-claude-omc] $*"; }
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Canonical OMC marketplace URL — matches the host machine's settings.json.
OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL="https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"

npm_g() {  # global npm install with sudo fallback (image prefix is root-owned)
  npm install -g "$@" 2>/dev/null || sudo npm install -g "$@"
}

# 1. Claude Code + omc CLI: update to latest (npm, matching the image install);
#    if npm is somehow unavailable, fall back to the native installer, which
#    puts a per-user binary in ~/.local/bin.
if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing/updating Claude Code + omc CLI (npm -g)"
  npm_g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    || log "WARN: npm -g install failed"
fi
if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "claude not on PATH; trying native installer"
  curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash || log "WARN: native install failed"
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi
if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "ERROR: claude still not on PATH — aborting (omc setup needs it)"
  exit 1
fi
log "claude: $(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1)"

# 2. oh-my-claudecode plugin — provides the /oh-my-claudecode:* skills.
#    marketplace add fails harmlessly if it is already registered.
log "wiring oh-my-claudecode plugin"
claude plugin marketplace add "$OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL" 2>/dev/null || true
claude plugin marketplace update omc || true
claude plugin install oh-my-claudecode@omc || log "WARN: omc plugin install failed"

# 3. omc setup — installs the HUD statusline wrapper, hooks, agents and skills
#    into ~/.claude.
if command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "running omc setup (HUD + hooks + agents + skills)"
  omc setup --quiet || log "WARN: omc setup failed"
else
  log "WARN: omc CLI unavailable; HUD/hooks may be incomplete"
fi

# 4. Merge the host's Claude niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json (jq merge,
#    existing keys survive). bypassPermissions is container-specific (sandboxed
#    vscode user); DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER because the npm -g install is root-owned
#    — updates happen by re-running this script, not by claude self-updating.
mkdir -p ~/.claude
SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
[ -s "$SETTINGS" ] || echo '{}' > "$SETTINGS"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  jq \
    '.permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"
     | .env["CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS"] = "1"
     | .env["DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER"] = "1"
     | .statusLine = {"type": "command", "command": "node ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hud/omc-hud.mjs"}
     | .enabledPlugins["oh-my-claudecode@omc"] = true
     | .extraKnownMarketplaces.omc.source = {"source": "git", "url": "https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"}
     | .editorMode = "vim"
     | .verbose = true
     | .teammateMode = "tmux"
     | .tui = "fullscreen"' \
    "$SETTINGS" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$SETTINGS"
  log "merged HUD + OMC niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json"
else
  log "WARN: jq missing; could not write ~/.claude/settings.json"
fi

log "done — run scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh to verify"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Health check for the devcontainer: verifies everything the container is
# supposed to ship (claude, omc, plugin, HUD, uv, .venv) and prints the fix
# for anything missing. Exits non-zero if any check fails.
#
#   scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh
set -uo pipefail
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

FAIL=0
ok()   { printf '  \033[32mok\033[0m    %s\n' "$1"; }
bad()  { printf '  \033[31mFAIL\033[0m  %s\n      fix: %s\n' "$1" "$2"; FAIL=1; }

echo "devcontainer doctor"

command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && ok "node $(node --version)" \
  || bad "node missing" "rebuild the devcontainer (Dockerfile installs Node LTS)"

command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && ok "claude $(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1)" \
  || bad "claude missing" "scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh"

command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && ok "omc $(command -v omc)" \
  || bad "omc CLI missing" "scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh"

if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  claude plugin list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi 'oh-my-claudecode' \
    && ok "oh-my-claudecode plugin installed" \
    || bad "oh-my-claudecode plugin missing" "scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh"
fi

[ -f "$HOME/.claude/hud/omc-hud.mjs" ] \
  && ok "OMC HUD statusline (~/.claude/hud/omc-hud.mjs)" \
  || bad "OMC HUD missing" "omc setup   (or scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh)"

[ -s "$HOME/.claude/settings.json" ] && grep -q statusLine "$HOME/.claude/settings.json" 2>/dev/null \
  && ok "~/.claude/settings.json has statusLine" \
  || bad "~/.claude/settings.json not wired" "scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh"

command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && ok "uv $(uv --version 2>/dev/null)" \
  || bad "uv missing" "curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh"

[ -x .venv/bin/python ] \
  && ok ".venv ($(.venv/bin/python --version 2>&1))" \
  || bad ".venv missing" "uv sync --extra viz"

if [ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "all checks passed"
else
  echo "some checks FAILED — run the fixes above, then re-run this script"
fi
exit "$FAIL"

# Runs once on container create/rebuild. Sequential + idempotent so the whole
# environment (uv, deps, Claude Code, oh-my-claudecode, HUD, hooks, shell) is
# set up automatically with no manual steps. Safe to re-run.
#

# script fails; scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh (step 3) updates them and wires the
# plugin/HUD/settings, and can be re-run standalone. Verify any time with
# scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh.
set -uo pipefail
log() { echo "[post-create] $*"; }
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# 1. uv (for the vscode user; the Dockerfile installs it for root)
if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing uv"
  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi

# 2. Project dependencies — uv sync creates the project-local .venv (python
#    pinned by .python-version) with the dev dependency-group. The viz extra
#    adds kedro-viz for the pipeline graph on port 4141 (auto-forwarded).
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then
  log "installing project deps (uv sync --extra viz)"
  uv sync --extra viz || log "WARN: uv sync failed"
fi

# 2b. VisiData — interactive terminal explorer for parquet/csv/jsonl artifacts.
#     Installed isolated via `uv tool` so it never touches the project venv.
if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing visidata (uv tool)"
  uv tool install 'visidata[parquet]' 2>/dev/null \
    || uv tool install visidata \
    || log "WARN: visidata install failed (non-fatal)"
fi

# 3. Claude Code + oh-my-claudecode — update CLIs, install the OMC plugin, run
#    `omc setup` (HUD/hooks/agents/skills), merge ~/.claude/settings.json.
if [ -x scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh ] || [ -f scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh ]; then
  bash scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh \
    || log "WARN: claude/omc setup incomplete — re-run scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh"
else
  log "WARN: scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh missing; claude/omc left at image versions"
fi

# 4. pre-commit git hooks (only if the repo defines them)
if [ -f .pre-commit-config.yaml ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing pre-commit hooks"
  uv run pre-commit install || log "WARN: pre-commit install failed"
fi

mkdir -p ~/.config/dev-bootstrap
cat > ~/.config/dev-bootstrap/commands.txt <<'EOF'
source .venv/bin/activate            # activate the project venv
make check                           # lint + typecheck + test
make build-sample                    # build the sample index (configs/tiny.yaml)
make search-sample                   # hybrid search over the sample index

vd artifacts/sample                  # browse index artifacts (VisiData)
scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh       # verify claude/omc/uv/.venv are healthy
scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh          # (re)install/update Claude Code + OMC
EOF

# 6. Shell: link the shared dotfiles (zshrc / starship / tmux) from ~/env.
#    ~/env is bind-mounted read-only from the host (see devcontainer.json), so a
#    single source of truth drives the host and every container.
ENV_DIR="$HOME/env"
if [ -x "$ENV_DIR/install.sh" ]; then
  log "linking dotfiles from $ENV_DIR"
  "$ENV_DIR/install.sh" --link || log "WARN: dotfile link failed"
else
  log "NOTE: ~/env not mounted; using default shell config"
fi

# 7. zsh-history-substring-search (not packaged on Debian)
HSS="$HOME/.zsh/plugins/zsh-history-substring-search"
[ -d "$HSS" ] || git clone --depth=1 \
  https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-history-substring-search "$HSS" || true

log "done — run scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh to verify"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs once on container create/rebuild. Sequential + idempotent so the whole
# environment (uv, deps, Claude Code, oh-my-claudecode, HUD, hooks, shell) is
# set up automatically with no manual steps. Safe to re-run.
set -uo pipefail
log() { echo "[post-create] $*"; }
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Canonical OMC marketplace URL — matches the host machine's settings.json.
OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL="https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"

# 1. uv (for the vscode user; the Dockerfile installs it for root)
if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing uv"
  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi

# 2. Project dependencies — a project-local .venv the scripts/launch.json expect
#    (.venv/bin/python). Install the package editable with the dev + notebooks
#    extras, plus oracledb (thick-mode driver for the live TIA/Oracle pull; it
#    is imported by src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/.../oracle_source.py but not pinned in the
#    project metadata, so we add it explicitly). This mirrors the working host
#    venv (kedro-viz, plotly, ipykernel, pytest, s3fs, oracledb all present).
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then
  log "creating .venv (python 3.12)"
  uv venv --python 3.12 || log "WARN: uv venv failed"
  log "installing project + dev,notebooks extras + oracledb"
  uv pip install -e ".[dev,notebooks]" oracledb || log "WARN: dependency install failed"
fi

# 2b. VisiData — interactive terminal explorer for the pipeline's data artifacts
#     (parquet findings/intermediates, xlsx golden masters, csv drilldowns).
#     Installed isolated via `uv tool` so it never touches the project venv.
if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing visidata (uv tool)"
  uv tool install 'visidata[parquet]' 2>/dev/null \
    || uv tool install visidata \
    || log "WARN: visidata install failed (non-fatal)"
fi

# 2d. nbstripout git filter — .gitattributes marks *.ipynb/*.zpln with
#     filter=nbstripout, but the clean/smudge commands live in the per-clone
#     .git/config (not the repo). Point them at THIS container's .venv python so
#     notebook outputs are stripped on commit. `--install` is idempotent and
#     rewrites any stale absolute path from a previous machine. nbstripout ships
#     in the notebooks extra installed above.
if [ -f pyproject.toml ] && [ -x .venv/bin/python ] && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "configuring nbstripout git filter (.venv)"
  .venv/bin/python -m nbstripout --install --attributes .gitattributes \
    || log "WARN: nbstripout filter install failed"
fi

# 3. Claude Code (install or update to latest)
log "installing/updating Claude Code (latest)"
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash || log "WARN: claude install failed"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# 4. oh-my-claudecode plugin (latest) — provides the /oh-my-claudecode:* skills
if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "setting up oh-my-claudecode plugin"
  claude plugin marketplace add "$OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL" || log "WARN: omc marketplace add failed"
  claude plugin marketplace update omc || true
  claude plugin install oh-my-claudecode@omc || log "WARN: omc plugin install failed"
else
  log "WARN: claude not on PATH; skipping oh-my-claudecode plugin"
fi

# 5. omc CLI + `omc setup` — installs the HUD statusline wrapper, hooks, agents
#    and skills into ~/.claude (the piece that gives the host its HUD niceties).
#    The CLI is baked into the image (Dockerfile); install per-user if missing.
if ! command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing omc CLI (oh-my-claude-sisyphus)"
  npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest 2>/dev/null \
    || sudo npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    || log "WARN: omc CLI install failed"
fi
if command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "running omc setup (HUD + hooks + agents + skills)"
  omc setup --quiet || log "WARN: omc setup failed"
else
  log "WARN: omc CLI unavailable; HUD/hooks may be incomplete"
fi

# 6. pre-commit git hooks (only if the repo defines them)
if [ -f .pre-commit-config.yaml ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing pre-commit hooks"
  uv run pre-commit install || log "WARN: pre-commit install failed"
fi

# 6a. Azure CLI + azure-devops extension — the repo lives on
#     dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice, so `az repos pr` / `az pipelines` /
#     `az boards` is the terminal path to PRs, builds and work items
#     (gh only speaks GitHub). Idempotent: skipped when already installed.
if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing Azure CLI"
  curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash || log "WARN: azure-cli install failed"
fi
if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! az extension show --name azure-devops >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "adding azure-devops extension"
  az extension add --name azure-devops || log "WARN: azure-devops extension install failed"
fi

# 6b. Azure DevOps CLI defaults — org/project set once so no command needs
#     flags. Auth: export AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (e.g. via the repo's .env) for
#     non-interactive use, or `az login` / `az devops login` interactively.
if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "configuring az devops org/project defaults"
  az devops configure --defaults \
    organization=https://dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice \
    "project=Data Science and Advanced Analytics" \
    || log "WARN: az devops configure failed"
else
  log "WARN: az not on PATH (azure-cli feature missing?); skipping ADO defaults"
fi

# 6c. Azure DevOps aliases — oh-my-zsh sources every $ZSH_CUSTOM/*.zsh file.
ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR="${ZSH_CUSTOM:-$HOME/.oh-my-zsh/custom}"
if [ -d "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR" ]; then
  log "writing azure-devops aliases ($ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh)"
  cat > "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh" <<'EOF'
# Azure DevOps shortcuts (org/project defaults set by post-create.sh)
alias adopr='az repos pr create --draft --open'      # current branch -> draft PR
alias adoprs='az repos pr list --status active -o table'
alias adoruns='az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table'
EOF
fi

# 7. Handy command cheatsheet (shown by ~/.zshrc on interactive login)
mkdir -p ~/.config/dev-bootstrap
cat > ~/.config/dev-bootstrap/commands.txt <<'EOF'
source .venv/bin/activate            # activate the project venv
scripts/run.sh offline               # rebuild ledgers + deliverables (no DB)
scripts/run.sh full                  # live TIA + Django pull -> ledgers -> deliverables
kedro run --pipeline figures         # just redraw the two infographics
kedro viz                            # interactive pipeline graph (port 4141, auto-forwarded)
scripts/run_notebooks.sh             # rerun the audit notebooks (notebook<->pipeline smoke test)
pytest -q                            # reconciliation + source-contract gates
python -m policy_schedule_data_pipeline.core.data_paths          # which window/pull is current
duckdb -c "select outcome, count(*) n from 'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1 order by n desc"
vd data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet                   # browse the ledger (VisiData)
yq '.tia_log' src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/reference/source_queries.yaml   # the SQL, as owned data
az repos pr create --draft --open    # current branch -> draft PR (alias: adopr)
az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table  # recent pipeline runs (alias: adoruns)
# A live pull needs TIA_PASSWORD + PG_DJANGO_PROD_PASSWORD (both in .env).
# ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB is preset to the Instant Client baked into this image.
# NOTE: a full pull re-reads the MUTABLE TIA.POLICY, which re-dates the
# landed / phantom / MTA numbers on every artifact. Offline runs never do.
EOF

# 8. Mirror the host's Claude niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json.
#    Merged via jq so existing keys survive. This wires:
#      - HUD statusline        - agent teams (needs tmux, in image)
#      - vim editor mode       - tmux teammates + fullscreen TUI
#      - verbose output        - the OMC plugin + marketplace
#    plus bypassPermissions, which is container-specific (sandboxed vscode user).
mkdir -p ~/.claude
SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
[ -s "$SETTINGS" ] || echo '{}' > "$SETTINGS"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  jq \
    '.permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"
     | .env["CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS"] = "1"
     | .statusLine = {"type": "command", "command": "node ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hud/omc-hud.mjs"}
     | .enabledPlugins["oh-my-claudecode@omc"] = true
     | .extraKnownMarketplaces.omc.source = {"source": "git", "url": "https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"}
     | .editorMode = "vim"
     | .verbose = true
     | .teammateMode = "tmux"
     | .tui = "fullscreen"' \
    "$SETTINGS" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$SETTINGS"
  log "merged HUD + OMC niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json"
else
  log "WARN: jq missing; could not write ~/.claude/settings.json"
fi

# 9. Shell: link the shared dotfiles (zshrc / starship / tmux) from ~/env.
#    ~/env is bind-mounted read-only from the host (see devcontainer.json), so a
#    single source of truth drives the host and every container.
ENV_DIR="$HOME/env"
if [ -x "$ENV_DIR/install.sh" ]; then
  log "linking dotfiles from $ENV_DIR"
  "$ENV_DIR/install.sh" --link || log "WARN: dotfile link failed"
else
  log "NOTE: ~/env not mounted; using default shell config"
fi

# 10. zsh-history-substring-search (not packaged on Debian)
HSS="$HOME/.zsh/plugins/zsh-history-substring-search"
[ -d "$HSS" ] || git clone --depth=1 \
  https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-history-substring-search "$HSS" || true

log "done"

Done. The devcontainer will now always build with `claude` and `omc`, and the setup logic lives in re-runnable scripts under `./scripts`.

**Why claude was missing:** it was only installed in `post-create.sh` via `curl https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash || log "WARN: ..."` — a swallowed failure. Worse, an earlier step in that script ran `uv pip install -e ".[dev,notebooks]"`, which fails in this repo (those extras don't exist here — the whole `.devcontainer` was copied from `policy-schedule-data-pipeline`), so the script was already limping by the time it got to Claude.

**What changed:**

- **`.devcontainer/Dockerfile`** — Claude Code is now installed system-wide at image build time (`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest` alongside the existing `omc` install), with `command -v claude && command -v omc` so a failed install fails the image build instead of surfacing weeks later. Even if post-create dies completely, the container has both CLIs.
- **`scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh`** (new) — updates both CLIs, adds the OMC marketplace, installs the `oh-my-claudecode@omc` plugin, runs `omc setup` (HUD/hooks/agents/skills), and merges your settings niceties into `~/.claude/settings.json`. It also sets `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` since the npm install is root-owned — re-run this script to update instead. Idempotent; run it any time inside the container.
- **`scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh`** (new) — pass/fail health check (node, claude, omc, plugin, HUD, settings, uv, .venv) with the fix printed next to each failure. Verified working: it correctly flagged that your Mac host lacks the `omc` CLI while everything else passed.
- **`.devcontainer/post-create.sh`** — rewritten for this repo: deps install via `uv sync --extra viz` (verified it resolves; viz gives you kedro-viz on the forwarded port 4141), Claude/OMC delegated to the new script, and the login cheatsheet now shows cybernaut-mini commands (`make check`, `make build-sample`, etc.). I dropped the steps that belonged to the other project: nbstripout (no `.gitattributes` here), and the Azure DevOps org defaults/aliases pointing at `OMIDataOffice`.

All scripts pass `bash -n`, the jq merge was tested to preserve existing settings keys, and `devcontainer.json` still parses. Rebuild the container and run `scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh` to confirm — everything should be green.

One flag: the Dockerfile still carries heavy baggage from the other project — Oracle Instant Client, AWS CLI v2 + `aws-azure-login` + chromium, and the `azure-cli` feature in `devcontainer.json`. Nothing in cybernaut-mini uses any of it, and stripping it would cut the image build time substantially. Say the word and I'll trim it.

# .devcontainer/Dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \
    libgomp1 \
    libaio1 \
    graphviz \
    zsh \
    tmux \
    neovim \
    btop \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Oracle Instant Client (basiclite) — python-oracledb THICK mode needs it.
# TIA QA (tiafsqa) is older than 12.1 and resets THIN connections (DPY-4011),
# so the live pull runs thick, exactly like DBeaver's OCI driver. The pipeline
# reads $ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB (conf/base/parameters.yml -> oracle.lib_dir); we set
# it below and register the lib dir with ldconfig so LD_LIBRARY_PATH is optional.
# libaio1 (installed above) is the only shared-lib dependency.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linuxx64.zip" ;; \
      arm64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linux-arm64.zip" ;; \
      *) url="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$url" ]; then \
      mkdir -p /opt/oracle; \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$tmp/ic.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/ic.zip" -d /opt/oracle; \
      ln -sfn "$(find /opt/oracle -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'instantclient_*' | head -1)" /opt/oracle/instantclient; \
      echo /opt/oracle/instantclient > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/oracle-instantclient.conf; \
      ldconfig; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no Oracle Instant Client build for arch=$arch; thick mode unavailable"; \
    fi
ENV ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB=/opt/oracle/instantclient

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Claude Code + oh-my-claudecode CLI (system-wide) — baked into the IMAGE so
# `claude` and `omc` exist even if post-create fails or is skipped. post-create
# (via scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh) updates both to latest and wires the OMC
# plugin/HUD/hooks; the npm prefix is root-owned so the settings merge disables
# claude's self-updater (updates go through the setup script instead).
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    && command -v claude && command -v omc

# AWS session tooling — so the Azure-federated STS login can be refreshed FROM
# INSIDE this container, not only on the WSL host. The artifact root is S3
# (PSDP_DATA_ROOT) with 12h tokens, so "my session died mid-session" is routine;
# previously it meant dropping out to a host terminal. See scripts/azlogin.
#
#   aws CLI v2       : `aws sts get-caller-identity` is how scripts/az_login.sh
#                      authoritatively verifies a login (the tool's exit code
#                      lies), plus general S3 work against the artifact root.
#   chromium (apt)   : NOT used as the browser — puppeteer ships its own
#                      version-matched build. This is here for its shared-library
#                      dependencies (libnss3/libgbm1/libasound2/…), which that
#                      bundled Chromium needs; the binary is a fallback you can
#                      select with PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium.
#   aws-azure-login  : the SAML login itself. Pinned — 3.6.x is what the login
#                      flow in scripts/az_login.sh is written against.
#
# The npm install is guarded: puppeteer's postinstall is what fetches that
# matched Chromium, and npm 11 already warns that the script is "not yet covered
# by allowScripts". It still runs today, but the day it stops, .local-chromium is
# silently empty and the login breaks at runtime, in the user's terminal, weeks
# later. --foreground-scripts puts the download in the build log and the `test -d`
# turns that failure into a failed image build instead.
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) a="x86_64" ;; \
      arm64) a="aarch64" ;; \
      *) a="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$a" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-${a}.zip" -o "$tmp/awscliv2.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/awscliv2.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      "$tmp/aws/install" --update; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no AWS CLI v2 build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi; \
    npm install -g --foreground-scripts aws-azure-login@3.6.4; \
    test -d /usr/lib/node_modules/aws-azure-login/node_modules/puppeteer/.local-chromium

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Data-pipeline CLI tooling — chosen for THIS project's artifacts:
#   duckdb : SQL straight over the pipeline's parquet/csv/xlsx without Python —
#            e.g. duckdb -c "select status,count(*) from
#            'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1"
#   yq     : query/validate the owned SQL + taxonomy YAML (source_queries /
#            error_taxonomy / scope) from the shell, jq-style.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) duck="amd64"; yqa="amd64" ;; \
      arm64) duck="arm64"; yqa="arm64" ;; \
      *) duck=""; yqa="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$duck" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/latest/download/duckdb_cli-linux-${duck}.zip" -o "$tmp/duckdb.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/duckdb.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$tmp/duckdb" /usr/local/bin/duckdb; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_${yqa}" -o /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no duckdb/yq build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi

# eza / delta / dust (not in Debian stable) + starship prompt.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) t="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      arm64) t="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      *) t="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$t" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/eza-community/eza/releases/latest/download/eza_${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/0.18.2/delta-0.18.2-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/bootandy/dust/releases/download/v1.1.1/dust-v1.1.1-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name eza   | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/eza; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name delta | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/delta; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name dust  | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/dust; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    fi; \
    curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y

RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip

# .devcontainer/Dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \
    libgomp1 \
    graphviz \
    zsh \
    tmux \
    neovim \
    btop \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Claude Code + oh-my-claudecode CLI (system-wide) — baked into the IMAGE so
# `claude` and `omc` exist even if post-create fails or is skipped. post-create
# (via scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh) updates both to latest and wires the OMC
# plugin/HUD/hooks; the npm prefix is root-owned so the settings merge disables
# claude's self-updater (updates go through the setup script instead).
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    && command -v claude && command -v omc

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Data CLI tooling:
#   duckdb : SQL straight over the corpus/artifacts without Python —
#            e.g. duckdb -c "select count(*) from 'data/sample/documents.jsonl'"
#   yq     : query/validate the YAML configs (configs/*.yaml, conf/base/*)
#            from the shell, jq-style.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) duck="amd64"; yqa="amd64" ;; \
      arm64) duck="arm64"; yqa="arm64" ;; \
      *) duck=""; yqa="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$duck" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/latest/download/duckdb_cli-linux-${duck}.zip" -o "$tmp/duckdb.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/duckdb.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$tmp/duckdb" /usr/local/bin/duckdb; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_${yqa}" -o /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no duckdb/yq build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi

# eza / delta / dust (not in Debian stable) + starship prompt.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) t="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      arm64) t="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      *) t="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$t" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/eza-community/eza/releases/latest/download/eza_${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/0.18.2/delta-0.18.2-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/bootandy/dust/releases/download/v1.1.1/dust-v1.1.1-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name eza   | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/eza; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name delta | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/delta; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name dust  | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/dust; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    fi; \
    curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y

RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## huggingface
You have tools for using the Hugging Face Hub. Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'neelan'
hf:// URIs can be converted to browser URLs by replacing hf://buckets/OWNER/NAME/PATH with https://huggingface.co/buckets/OWNER/NAME/resolve/PATH; for models, datasets, and spaces, use https://huggingface.co[/datasets|/spaces]/OWNER/NAME/resolve/main/PATH. URL-encode each path segment. arXiv paper id's are often used as references between datasets, models and papers. There are over 100 tags in use, common tags include 'Text Generation', 'Transformers', 'Image Classification' and so on.

#!/usr/bin/env zsh
# =============================================================================
#  ~/.zshrc  —  cross-platform (macOS + Linux / devcontainer)
#  Canonical source: ~/env (https://github.com/neeland/env). Symlinked by install.sh.
#  Prompt: Powerlevel10k.  Tools auto-enable the moment they appear on PATH.
# =============================================================================

### 0. Platform detection -----------------------------------------------------
case "$OSTYPE" in
  darwin*) OMC_OS=mac   ;;
  *)       OMC_OS=linux ;;
esac
[[ -n "$REMOTE_CONTAINERS" || -n "$CODESPACES" || -f /.dockerenv ]] && OMC_IN_CONTAINER=1

### 1. Locale / editor --------------------------------------------------------
export LANG=${LANG:-en_US.UTF-8}
export LC_ALL=${LC_ALL:-$LANG}
if command -v nvim >/dev/null 2>&1; then export EDITOR=nvim; else export EDITOR=vim; fi
export VISUAL=$EDITOR

### 2. PATH: user-local bins + uv ---------------------------------------------
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
[[ -f "$HOME/.local/bin/env" ]] && . "$HOME/.local/bin/env"   # uv's env

### 3. macOS-only PATH bits (Homebrew is set in ~/.zprofile) ------------------
if [[ $OMC_OS == mac ]]; then
  [[ -x /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]] && eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
  [[ -d "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Coursier/bin" ]] && \
    export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/Library/Application Support/Coursier/bin"
  [[ -d "$HOME/.codeium/windsurf/bin" ]] && \
    export PATH="$HOME/.codeium/windsurf/bin:$PATH"
fi

### 4. History ----------------------------------------------------------------
HISTFILE=~/.zsh_history
HISTSIZE=50000
SAVEHIST=50000
setopt EXTENDED_HISTORY HIST_IGNORE_ALL_DUPS HIST_REDUCE_BLANKS \
       SHARE_HISTORY INC_APPEND_HISTORY

### 5. Shell options ----------------------------------------------------------
setopt AUTO_CD AUTO_PUSHD PUSHD_IGNORE_DUPS NO_BEEP INTERACTIVE_COMMENTS

### 6. Completion (cached; rebuilt at most once a day) ------------------------
() {
  setopt local_options extended_glob
  local dump="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/zsh/zcompdump"
  mkdir -p "${dump:h}"
  autoload -Uz compinit
  if [[ -n "$dump"(#qN.mh+24) ]]; then compinit -d "$dump"; else compinit -C -d "$dump"; fi
}
zstyle ':completion:*' use-cache on
zstyle ':completion:*' cache-path "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/zsh"
zstyle ':completion:*' matcher-list 'm:{a-zA-Z}={A-Za-z}'
zstyle ':completion:*' menu select

### 7. Modern CLI tools (auto-enabled when present) ---------------------------
if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  alias ls='eza --group-directories-first --icons=auto'
  alias ll='eza -lh  --group-directories-first --icons=auto --git'
  alias la='eza -lah --group-directories-first --icons=auto --git'
  alias lt='eza --tree --level=2 --icons=auto'
else
  alias ll='ls -lh'; alias la='ls -lah'
fi

if command -v bat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  alias cat='bat --paging=never'
elif command -v batcat >/dev/null 2>&1; then        # Debian names it batcat
  alias bat='batcat'; alias cat='batcat --paging=never'
fi

command -v dust   >/dev/null 2>&1 && alias du='dust'
command -v fd     >/dev/null 2>&1 || { command -v fdfind >/dev/null 2>&1 && alias fd='fdfind'; }
if command -v delta >/dev/null 2>&1; then           # side-by-side git diffs
  export GIT_PAGER='delta'
  export DELTA_FEATURES='+side-by-side line-numbers'
fi

### 8. fzf — fuzzy finder (Ctrl-R history, Ctrl-T file, Alt-C cd) -------------
if command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if fzf --zsh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    source <(fzf --zsh)                              # fzf >= 0.48
  else
    for f in /usr/share/doc/fzf/examples/key-bindings.zsh \
             /usr/share/fzf/key-bindings.zsh; do [[ -f $f ]] && source "$f"; done
    for f in /usr/share/doc/fzf/examples/completion.zsh \
             /usr/share/fzf/completion.zsh;   do [[ -f $f ]] && source "$f"; done
  fi
fi

### 9. zoxide — smarter cd (z / zi) ------------------------------------------
command -v zoxide >/dev/null 2>&1 && eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"

### 10. Powerlevel10k prompt -------------------------------------------------
# Enable Powerlevel10k instant prompt. Should stay close to the top of ~/.zshrc.
# Initialization code that may require console input (password prompts, [y/n]
# confirmations, etc.) must go above this block; everything else may go below.
if [[ -r "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh" ]]; then
  source "${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/p10k-instant-prompt-${(%):-%n}.zsh"
fi

# Load Powerlevel10k theme
[[ -f /opt/homebrew/share/powerlevel10k/powerlevel10k.zsh-theme ]] && \
  source /opt/homebrew/share/powerlevel10k/powerlevel10k.zsh-theme
[[ -f /usr/share/powerlevel10k/powerlevel10k.zsh-theme ]] && \
  source /usr/share/powerlevel10k/powerlevel10k.zsh-theme

    unset -f nvm node npm npx pnpm yarn 2>/dev/null
    source "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

    unset -f conda

export UV_LINK_MODE=copy
[[ -n "$OMC_IN_CONTAINER" ]] && export AWS_PROFILE="${AWS_PROFILE:-default}"

[[ -f "$PWD/.venv/bin/activate" ]] && source "$PWD/.venv/bin/activate"

### 14. General aliases & helpers --------------------------------------------
alias reload='exec zsh'
alias ..='cd ..'
alias ...='cd ../..'
alias path='echo $PATH | tr ":" "\n"'
alias gs='git status'
if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  alias k='uv run kedro'
